statement: A party cannot acquire prescriptive title to land if they have not been in possession of the land for more than 50 years.
supporting_quote: None of the said documents establish the prescriptive title of the Appellants.

statement: The burden of proof rests squarely and fairly on a party invoking the provisions of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance to defeat the ownership of an adverse claimant to immovable property to establish a starting point for their acquisition of prescriptive rights.
supporting_quote: Where a party invokes the provisions of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance in order to defeat the ownership of an adverse claimant to immovable property, the burden of proof rests squarely and fairly on him to establish a starting point for his or her acquisition of prescriptive rights.

statement: A principal servitude is considered abandoned if the accessory servitude is also abandoned.
supporting_quote: Servitudes are indivisible in their nature and where there are two servitudes-the one principal and the other accessory, which are due at the same time-and the principal is abandoned, the accessory also is regarded as abandoned

statement: In an action by a lessor against an overholding lessee for restoration and ejectment, privity of contract is the foundation of the right to relief, and issues as to title are irrelevant to the proceedings.
supporting_quote: Privity of contract (whether it be by original agreement or by attornment) is the foundation of the right to relief and issues as to title are irrelevant to the proceedings.

statement: A plaintiff can claim prescriptive title to land if they have been in uninterrupted possession of the land for ten years, without paying rent or performing any service or duty, and without acknowledging the rights of another person.
supporting_quote: This position in law is supported by many authorities. Maasdorp's Institutes (7th Edition Vol2 at 96) Wigneswaran J in Leisa and another V Simon and Another [2002 (1) SLR 148] Pathirana V Jayasundera [58 NLR 169] Dona Cecilia V Cecilia Perera and others [1987 (1) SLR 235] Wijesundara and others v Constantine Dasa and another [1987 (2) SLR 66] I will now turn to consider whether the learned District Judge correctly evaluated the evidence and applied the law relevant thereto when he accepted the prescriptive rights .I 3 of the plaintiff rejecting the defence taken up by the defendant.

statement: A party invoking the provisions of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance to defeat ownership must establish a starting point for their acquisition of prescriptive rights.
supporting_quote: lt is trite law that where a party to an action for a declaration of title to a land invokes the Provisions of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance in order to defeat the ownership of an adverse claimant to immovable property, the burden of proof rests squarely and fairly on him to establish a starting point for his or her acquisition of prescriptive rights.

statement: The owner or owners of the servient tenement over which a right of way is claimed in the pleadings must always be made a party to an action seeking a declaration of a right of way over that servient tenement.
supporting_quote: The owner or owners of the servient tenements over which a right of way is claimed in the pleadings must always be made a party to an action seeking a declaration of a right of way over that servient tenement (b) The owner or owners of a servient tenement over which a right of way merely passes need to be made a party to an action seeking a declaration of a right of way only where that party has specifically denied or objected to the existence of the plaintiff's right of way or obstructed it

statement: A duty is cast upon the Judge hearing a partition action to follow the provisions contained in the Partition Law.
supporting_quote: In this instance, action is filed to partition a land in extent of four bushels paddy sowing which is equivalent to 2 Acres of land in extent in accordance with the accepted measurement standards of conversion. The commissioner, who surveyed the land, has reported to Court that he could not state whether the land he surveyed is the land referred to in the schedule to the plaint or not. Upon considering the matters referred to above, it is clear that the land that had been surveyed is substantially different from the land described in the schedule to the plaint.

statement: A prescriptive title can be claimed if the respondent has been in possession of the land for a period of well over ten years prior to the filing of this action, adverse to the rights of the plaintiff.
supporting_quote: In the circumstances, it is abundantly clear that the respondent had been in possession of the land claimed by the plaintiff for a period of well over ten years prior to the filing of this action on 03.05.1991, adverse to the rights of the plaintiff which is the criteria applicable to claim prescriptive title in terms of Section 3 of the Prescription Ordinance.

statement: A certificate of sale does not divest the judgment-debtor's title to immovable property until the sale is confirmed by the court and a Fiscal's conveyance is executed.
supporting_quote: The right and title of the judgment-debtor or of any person holding under him or deriving title through him to immovable property sold by virtue of an execution is not divested by the sale until the confirmation of the sale by the court and the execution of the Fiscal's conveyance.

statement: There is no statutory bar to partition several lands held in common, but common ownership need to prevail in respect of all lands.
supporting_quote: There is no statutory bar to partition several lands held in Common. The deciding factor seems to be that common ownership need to prevail in respect of all lands.

statement: The transferee must hold the property for the benefit of the owner or his legal representative if it cannot be reasonably inferred that the owner intended to dispose of the beneficial interest.
supporting_quote: Where the owner of property transfers or bequeaths it, and it cannot reasonably be inferred consistently with the attendant circumstances that he intended to dispose of the beneficial interest therein, the transferee or legatee must hold such property for the benefit of the owner or his legal representative

statement: A claim for recovery of property belonging to a temple is not barred by prescription under the Prescription Ordinance.
supporting_quote: The Respondent's plea of prescription should necessarily fail.

statement: A notary is entitled to practice in a judicial zone, even if they reside in a different district, as long as the districts are within the same judicial zone.
supporting_quote: Every warrant issued to a notary under the provisions of section 3 or 4, authorizing him to practice as a notary in any judicial division in which he resides, shall be deemed to authorize him to practise as a notary in the judicial zone in which he resides.

statement: A party to a partition case cannot have the interlocutory decree set aside without being a party to the case.
supporting_quote: The petitioner not being a party to the partition case is not entitled to make an application under section 48 (4).

statement: A donor can revoke a deed of gift on the basis of ingratitude if the donee commits an atrocious injury to the donor.
supporting_quote: if the donee does atrocious injury to the donor it becomes a reason to have a deed of gift revoked.

statement: A tenant who fails to pay rent after a lease agreement expires becomes a trespasser and can be ejected.
supporting_quote: In such situation the Appellants become trespassers on the land and therefore a cause of action will accrue to the Respondents to claim the property back with damages caused to them.

statement: A possessor is always presumed to hold in his own right and as proprietor until the contrary be demonstrated.
supporting_quote: A possessor is always presumed to hold in his own right and as proprietor until the contrary be demonstrated;

statement: In effecting a partition, proper rights of way should be provided within the corpus to the district allotments as means of access to a public right of way.
supporting_quote: It is trite Law that in effecting a partition proper rights of way should be provided within the corpus to the district allotments as means of access to a public right of way.

statement: A court may grant an extension of time to file objections under section 91A(1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Code.
supporting_quote: Where a day is fixed or time appointed for doing any act or taking any proceeding by a party to the action, the court may, from time to time, upon the motions of such party and if sufficient cause is shown, fix another day or enlarge or abridge the time appointed, upon such terms, if any, as to it may seem proper.

statement: A Magistrate's Court should not be turned into a forum for the settlement of civil disputes, yet, a Magistrate making an order under Section 431 must exercise his judicial discretion in ascertaining the person entitled to possession.
supporting_quote: A Magistrate's Court should not be turned into a forum for the settlement of civil disputes, yet, a Magistrate making an order under Section 431 must exercise his judicial discretion in ascertaining the person entitled to possession.

statement: Once the notice of an application for acquisition of a property is issued by the Bank and registered in the relevant land registry, it is considered as an instrument affecting the premises, and until such notice is cancelled by the Bank, there will be an encumbrance on the said premises.
supporting_quote: Every notice under paragraph (b) shall be registered by the Registrar of Lands in the manner prescribed in the Registration of Documents Ordinance for the registration of an instrument affecting or relating to land and shall be deemed for such purposes to be an instrument affecting or relating to premises the prescribed particulars of which are set out in such notice.

statement: A government entity cannot bypass a valid lease agreement and deal directly with the lessee.
supporting_quote: On this background LRC bypassing the SLSPC and dealing with the petitioner is inappropriate.

statement: A Fiscal's sale of property subject to partition action is not held void so that debtors would not be encouraged to defraud creditors under the pretext of partition actions.
supporting_quote: A Fiscal's sale of property subject to partition action is not held void so that debtors would not be encouraged to defraud creditors under the pretext of partition actions (K.D.P. Wickramasinghe, Law of Partition in Ceylon at pg 201).

statement: A person can acquire prescriptive title to a land by being in exclusive possession of it as a separate entity for a period of well over 10 years.
supporting_quote: The fact that there were physical boundaries around the corpus also shows that the 3rd defendant did not possess the corpus. The 3rd defendant’s predecessor in title was in possession of the land adjoining to the corpus, which was separated by the said physical boundaries. In the circumstances, the conclusion that the plaintiffs and the 1st defendant had become in exclusive possession of the corpus adverse to the rights of the other co-owners of the larger land and had possessed the corpus as a separate entity of the land for a period of well over 10 years and acquired prescriptive title to the corpus was correct.
